claims.text: What the image looks like Transverse colon > 6 cm with thumbprinting → toxic megacolon (UC, C. difficile)
claims.quote: Transverse colon >6 cm with thumbprinting Toxic megacolon (UC, C. difficile)

claims.text: Flat and upright films may show megacolon or intraluminal gas over a long, continuous, paralyzed segment of colon (lost muscle tone)
claims.quote: Flat and upright abdominal radiographs should be taken; they may show megacolon or intraluminal gas accumulated over a long, continuous, paralyzed segment of colon—a result of lost muscle tone.

claims.text: Buzzword: thumbprinting (mucosal edema) on AXR / CT colon → ischemic / inflammatory colitis, toxic megacolon
claims.quote: Thumbprinting (mucosal edema) AXR / CT colon Ischemic / inflammatory colitis, toxic megacolon

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Megacolon is defined as a transverse colon > 6 cm during an exacerbation; Merck discourages the term toxic megacolon because the toxic state can occur without frank megacolon
claims.quote: The terms toxic megacolon and toxic dilation are discouraged because the toxic inflammatory state and its complications can occur without frank megacolon (defined as transverse colon > 6 cm diameter during an exacerbation).

claims.text: Large bowel: peripheral “picture frame”; haustra do NOT cross the full diameter; dilated > 6 cm (> 9 cm at the cecum)
claims.quote: Large bowel = peripheral 'picture frame', haustra do NOT cross full diameter, dilated >6 cm (>9 cm at cecum).

claims.text: Avoid barium enema (perforation risk); a careful sigmoidoscopy is typically advisable to assess severity and exclude infection
claims.quote: Barium enema should be avoided because of the risk of perforation, but a careful sigmoidoscopy is typically advisable to assess severity and exclude infection.

claims.text: Causes Toxic (fulminant) colitis: transmural extension of ulceration causes localized ileus and peritonitis; within hours to days the colon loses muscular tone and begins to dilate
claims.quote: Toxic colitis or fulminant colitis occurs when transmural extension of ulceration results in localized ileus and peritonitis. Within hours to days, the colon loses muscular tone and begins to dilate.

claims.text: A medical emergency, usually spontaneous in very severe colitis but sometimes precipitated by opioid or anticholinergic antidiarrheals; colonic perforation increases mortality significantly
claims.quote: Toxic colitis is a medical emergency that usually occurs spontaneously in the course of very severe colitis but is sometimes precipitated by opioid or anticholinergic antidiarrheal medications. Colonic perforation may occur, which increases mortality significantly.

claims.text: C. difficile toxins cause pseudomembranous colitis, typically after antibiotics; diarrhea, sometimes bloody, rarely progresses to toxic megacolon, colonic perforation, sepsis and acute abdomen
claims.quote: Toxins produced by Clostridioides difficile strains in the gastrointestinal tract cause pseudomembranous colitis, typically after antibiotic use. Symptoms are diarrhea, sometimes bloody, rarely progressing to toxic megacolon, colonic perforation, sepsis, and acute abdomen.

claims.text: Symptoms Initially: sudden violent diarrhea, fever to 40° C (104° F), abdominal pain, signs of peritonitis (eg, rebound tenderness) and profound toxemia
claims.quote: Toxic or fulminant colitis manifests initially with sudden violent diarrhea, fever to 40° C (104° F), abdominal pain, signs of peritonitis (eg, rebound tenderness), and profound toxemia.

claims.text: Picture when fulminant or toxic colitis is suspected: > 10 stools per day with continuous blood, colonic dilation with fever, tachycardia, anemia and elevated inflammatory markers
claims.quote: If fulminant or toxic colitis is suspected (>10 stools per day with continuous blood, colonic dilation with fever, tachycardia, anemia, and elevated inflammatory markers)

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: bowel rest, IV steroids; emergent colectomy if perforation
claims.quote: Bowel rest, IV steroids; emergent colectomy if perforation

claims.text: Stop all antidiarrheals; nothing by mouth with a long intestinal tube on intermittent suction; aggressive IV fluids and electrolytes (isotonic saline, potassium and blood as needed); high-dose IV glucocorticoids or cyclosporine; antibiotics (eg, metronidazole and ciprofloxacin); perhaps infliximab
claims.quote: Stop all antidiarrheal medications Take nothing by mouth and have inserted a long intestinal tube attached to intermittent suction Receive aggressive IV fluid and electrolyte therapy with isotonic saline, with potassium and blood as needed Receive high-dose IV glucocorticoids or cyclosporine Receive antibiotics (eg, metronidazole 500 mg IV every 6 to 8 hours and ciprofloxacin 500 mg IV every 12 hours) Perhaps receive infliximab

claims.text: No definite improvement on intensive medical measures within 24 to 48 hours → immediate surgery, or the patient may die of sepsis or perforation
claims.quote: If intensive medical measures do not produce definite improvement within 24 to 48 hours, immediate surgery is required or the patient may die of sepsis caused by bacterial translocation or even perforation.

claims.text: Emergency colectomy for massive hemorrhage, fulminating toxic colitis or perforation; usually subtotal colectomy with ileostomy and rectosigmoid closure (Hartmann procedure) or mucous fistula
claims.quote: Emergency colectomy is indicated for massive hemorrhage, fulminating toxic colitis, or perforation. Subtotal colectomy with ileostomy and rectosigmoid closure (Hartmann procedure) or mucous fistula is usually the procedure of choice because most critically ill patients cannot tolerate more extensive surgery.
